descriptionChirho: The state of being uncircumcised, used abstractly and metonymically in Pauline theology to designate Gentiles collectively or the condition of not having undergone the covenant rite of circumcision (Rom 2:25-27, 3:30, 4:9-12; 1 Cor 7:18-19; Gal 2:7, 5:6, 6:15; Eph 2:11; Col 2:13, 3:11). Nineteen of the 20 occurrences use this abstract/metonymic sense. Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'incircuncision,' Arabic 'al-ghurla' (الغرلة), Hindi 'khatnarahit' (खतनारहित), Korean 'muhallye' (무할례), Swahili 'kutokutahiriwa/wasiotahiriwa.'

The literal, anatomical foreskin (prepuce), referring to the physical tissue rather than the abstract state of being uncircumcised. The single occurrence (likely 1 Cor 7:18b, 'let him not become circumcised' implying physical reversal) uses the concrete bodily referent. Multilingual evidence distinguishes this from the abstract sense: Spanish 'prepucio' (not 'incircuncision'), Arabic 'ghurla' (غرلة, without the article), Korean 'popi-reul' (포피를, 'foreskin' with accusative marker), Swahili 'kutotahiriwa.' The shift from abstract condition to concrete anatomy justifies a separate sense.
